source_occurrence_map.source_boundary_note: Convolution uses positive spatial shifts; forward DFT uses negative phase. Preserve channel/grid dimensions and real-valued kernel/bias conventions.
Circular padding and stride one define the exact scope; this source condition is not an independent proved theorem.
Single-layer multi-channel h=Tg+delta MN b. Channel counts and circular scope remain explicit.

source_occurrence_map.author_label: Unnumbered activation-free theoretical network and ReLU applicability paragraph
source_occurrence_map.source_boundary_note: Author theoretical cascade omits activation functions; empirical verification on ReLU networks must not become an exact ReLU propagation theorem.
Full multi-channel cascade and DC bias beta; MN multiplies the whole bias bracket.
Equation (5) has conjugation on prefix T, input g, beta prime, derivative h and suffix T. Preserve transpose, eta MN, coupling chi and its quotient domain.

The source gives an argument from randomly initialized disjoint kernels, independent layers and the lottery-ticket hypothesis to early-epoch irrelevance; it is not solely a non-proof condition. Equations (6)/(7) state selected moment factorizations, not the same statement as independence of all products.
Source theorem here is single-channel, a complex product mean and log second moment; R is a sine quotient. Do not substitute the multi-channel formula for this statement.
Magnitude/SOM increases with four quantities: abs mean, abs R, kernel size and variance. The source list is not a numbered equation.
Retain exponential increase, independent log contributions, the LLN qualification, and the separate approximate multi-channel claim; a product formula alone does not establish every interpretation.
High-frequency weakening and stronger effect in deep networks, with the actual B.1 citation.
Large absolute mean makes high-frequency learning less likely, with B.2. Its source page is 6, not 5.
Small kernel makes high-frequency learning less likely, with B.3 and empirical verification qualification.
The printed second branch uses both edge conditions together. Retain the source definition, do not silently turn the AND into a complement/OR.
Main statement assumes each pixel marginal Gaussian and states a SOM difference plus DC equality; A.5 later uses i.i.d. Preserve both scopes.
Forward/backward propagation plus large tau squared at low frequencies is used to infer low-frequency preference. Keep this author explanation distinct from the exact SOM identity.
Width/height ratios and modular placement define the source operation; this is zero insertion, not an unspecified interpolation method.
Every channel/frequency repeats at the source ratio-indexed frequencies; preserve input/output dimensions.
Repeated fundamental frequencies are used to argue representation harm and possible real/generated discrimination; preserve the author may qualification.
Source setup uses a single-channel real image, A and conjugate A, alpha>0, phi<pi/2 only, real weights, and the identity baseline. Do not strengthen phase conditions.
Separate the literal one-gradient-step zero-loss clause from the proportional update norm. The main statement explicitly points to constraints (43)/(44), whose full context is in A.7.
Small frequency shift is used to infer large optimization cost and high learning difficulty; preserve its relation to the exact and proportional source claims.
External empirical low-frequency natural-image fact plus Corollaries 3.3/3.4 is used as an inference, repeated more fully in B.4; not just an experiment setting.
Author says different mean-biased layer positions have similar roles because of Corollary 3.3. C.8 supplies experimental results; keep the main mathematical explanation traceable.

source_occurrence_map.source_boundary_note: Exact cosine, low-frequency energy and pixel fitting definitions; PDF7 weight-change norm belongs to the separate shift/gradient targets.
Retain the all-real-theta quotient and root-of-unity special case, including limit reasoning; domain correction must remain separate from author source.
Distinct support equations used in subsequent proofs; do not omit because they have no separate theorem title.
Derivation first allows M prime,N prime and cross-frequency alpha. It is broader than the later circular specialization; preserve the full intermediate sum.
Source valid-convolution branch uses M-K+1,N-K+1 samples but prints M-K,N-K sine numerators. It is a different derivation from the circular theorem and remains a target.

source_occurrence_map.author_label: Circular coefficient and final h=Tg+delta MN b
source_occurrence_map.source_boundary_note: Same final object as main Theorem 3.2 after explicit circular specialization; preserve the source intermediate indices, rather than replacing them by a corrected final statement.
No new differently quantified theorem restatement. Full layer-by-layer proof includes source terminal indexing and an extra MN in one bias expansion; source and corrected proof cannot be conflated.

Complete real/imaginary CR reasoning, kernel-gradient transform, finite-support coupling, cascade chain rule and final update. Equation (24) first/second lines differ in the g conjugation bar; all original bars/transposes and normalizations retained.

Source disjoint-kernel/random-initialization and lottery-ticket extension argument is a genuine local argument; its early-training extrapolation remains separate from a rigorous initialization statement.

Source first replaces a real Gaussian by ComplexN(mu,sigma squared,0), then derives a generally nonzero response pseudocovariance. It is a proof-scope/object change to audit, not a repeated scalar moment statement.
Source log product and expectation recurrences support the main single-channel theorem; zero/positivity and independent-product scope still require mathematical review.

source_occurrence_map.author_label: Multi-channel product-matrix mean and SOM correction terms
source_occurrence_map.source_boundary_note: Different matrix-valued object from main single-channel theorem, with an explicit additional assumption on product-matrix elements. Keep the full multi-channel correction terms and the printed intermediate mu index.
No new theorem restatement; proof annotations add i.i.d. pixels at variance sums, absent from the marginal-Gaussian main statement. Retain this hypothesis change.
Same zero-insertion spectrum object as main. Full DC and periodic general-frequency calculations occupy both pages.
Specific source lambda, phase, total-response and bypass-square conditions are essential. Retain the original sufficient one-step claim; do not transfer the claim to an approximation silently.
Other-frequency updates (51)–(55), with Equation (55) on PDF26; selected-frequency updates (48)–(50) are separately linked to the one-step target.

Complete independent log-effect/LLN argument and almost certainly claim. It repeats and strengthens main conclusions (2)/(3), so preserve both locations and qualifications.
Actual imbalance argument repeats main conclusion (4), with its complete because/thereby reasoning.
